event.text: Nine B.C. First Nations announce Federal Court applications to quash the Pacific Link national-interest designation, saying Ottawa did not adequately consult them. Ottawa says it consulted more than 110 Indigenous communities and will offer a minimum 10 per cent ownership stake, The Globe and Mail and the Vancouver Sun report; Cold Lake First Nation filed the first challenge in October.

ops.find: The Major Projects Office aims to set the conditions for construction by September 1, 2027. On October 7 Cold Lake First Nations asked the Federal Court to quash the designation, saying it was not consulted.
ops.with: The Major Projects Office aims to have the conditions for construction in place by September 2027. On October 7 Cold Lake First Nations asked the Federal Court to quash the designation, saying it was not consulted; on November 2 nine B.C. First Nations announced they had filed their own applications.

ops.find: B.C. votes on October 24, and First Nations leaders meet the prime minister and premiers in Ottawa on October 26.
ops.with: The B.C. Conservatives won the October 24 provincial election, and First Nations leaders met the prime minister and most premiers in Ottawa on October 26.
